III. Teacher
Input

Ask students to discuss what they know about wind
and water as energy sources. Encourage them to
share what they wrote from the Problem of the Day
exercise.
Demonstrate how a pinwheel captures wind energy
using a desktop fan. Attach the pinwheel to the
shaft of the small DC motor. Attach the output of
the motor to either a low-voltage light bulb or a
multi-meter. The multimeter can demonstrate both
voltage and amperage (current) output. Blow the
desktop fan on the pinwheel.

(5 minutes)
 Straight pin or thumbtack
 Heavier paper e.g. cardstock
 Pencil with eraser
 Straight pin or thumbtack
 Small DC motor
 Insulated wire
 Light bulb (1.5V) and bulb holder
 Desktop fan
 Multi-meter (if available)

IV. Guided
Practice

In teams of three, the students will design and build
a pinwheel. They can choose from any of the
templates provided – at least three different
templates – or make their own. Encourage the
teams to make their designs artistic.
Allow teams to test their designs with the DC
motor and multi-meter if available. Teams will
record the voltage and current.

Links to pinwheel patterns (60 minutes)

images/art/PinwheelPattern.pdf

2011/07/tip-template-tuesday-6-
point-pinwheel.html

III. Guided
Practice

Show students the NASA YouTube Video: How
Gears Work
Show students the different gear types: Spur,
Worm, Bevel, Rack and Pinion, and Belt and
Pulley.
Ask students to see if they can name something
that shows each type of gear.

Computer and Projector (25 minutes)
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RSZ
vzVIyjYk
http://www.fi.edu/time/Journey/Time/E
scapements/geartypes.html
IV. Teacher Input

Ask students to discuss what gears they saw in
their homes yesterday.
Using Legos, students can build and demonstrate
the different types of gears (if available).
If Legos are unavailable, a bike can demonstrate
gear chains, or the back of a wall clock can suffice
as well.

Computer & Projector (5 minutes)
 Lego Kit (if available)
 Bike (if available)
 Wall clock
(25 minutes)
Lego Gears available at:
https://education.lego.com/en-us/lego-
education-product-database/machines-
and-mechanisms/9686-simple-and-
powered-machines-set
VI. Closure

Discuss the production process of Historic Yates
Mill County Park for cornmeal and flour and how
the waterwheel and gears play an essential role.

Computer & Projector
(7 minutes)
http://www.yatesmill.org/

II. Statement of
Objectives

―Tomorrow we will be going to Historic Yates Mill
County Park for a field trip. Today we will be
exploring some of the technology that we will see
there.‖
VI. Closure

Tomorrow we will be going on the field trip to Historic
Yates Mill County Park. Discuss details of trip
including departure times, what to bring, what to
expect, etc.

Computer and Projector
(15 minutes)
http://www.yatesmill.org/

IV. Guided
Practice

In groups of 4, have students brainstorm ways they can
make their own lunchroom/cafeteria more sustainable in as
many different ways as possible. Ideas include: food
production techniques: green energy milling, gardening;
recycling resources, minimizing trash, composting, etc.

Pencil & Paper
(30 minutes)
